subsystems.name: Diamond sensor element
subsystems.role: the sensing volume — a diamond containing nitrogen-vacancy centres whose spin state responds to magnetic field.

subsystems.name: Optical excitation
subsystems.role: green light pumps the NV centres into a known spin state.

subsystems.name: Microwave drive
subsystems.role: an applied microwave tone at about 2.87 GHz flips the electron spin; where it resonates reveals the local field.
parts: antenna loop or stripline on the diamond surface

subsystems.name: Fluorescence detection
subsystems.role: reads out the spin state through the brightness of red fluorescence.

subsystems.name: Bias field and shielding
subsystems.role: a small permanent magnet splits the spin levels so the response is linear and directional.
parts: magnetic shielding where ambient noise is severe

subsystems.name: Control and signal processing
subsystems.role: sweeps the microwaves, extracts the tiny dip in fluorescence and converts it to field values.

buildSteps.title: Grow the diamond
buildSteps.detail: Chemical vapour deposition builds diamond layer by layer from a methane-hydrogen plasma on a diamond seed. Nitrogen is added in controlled trace amounts, or the carbon is isotopically purified (carbon-12) to lengthen spin coherence.

buildSteps.title: Create the vacancies
buildSteps.detail: Electron irradiation or ion implantation knocks carbon atoms out of the lattice; a high-temperature anneal lets those vacancies migrate until they pair with nitrogen atoms, forming NV centres.

buildSteps.title: Shape the sensor
buildSteps.detail: The diamond is cut and polished, or etched into nanopillars and solid immersion lenses, so more of the fluorescence reaches the detector.

buildSteps.title: Add the microwave antenna
buildSteps.detail: A thin wire, loop or stripline is patterned onto or beside the diamond to deliver microwaves evenly across the sensing volume.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical head
buildSteps.detail: Laser, dichroic mirror, objective, filter and photodetector are aligned so green light enters and only red fluorescence is counted.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Known magnetic fields are applied and the microwave resonance splitting is measured, setting the sensitivity, linearity and axis alignment.

buildSteps.title: Package and deploy
buildSteps.detail: The head, bias magnet and electronics are integrated into an instrument, and software turns the fluorescence dip into a field reading or an image.

prerequisites.tech: CVD diamond growth with controlled nitrogen and isotopic purity
prerequisites.why: sensor performance depends on how many NV centres there are and how long their spin stays coherent.
that resonance is the readout mechanism, and it must be stable and quiet.
the signal is a small percentage change in fluorescence, so stray light and detector noise set the floor.

prerequisites.tech: Spin-control techniques (ODMR, spin echo, dynamical decoupling)
prerequisites.why: they extend coherence and let the sensor reject low-frequency noise.
a single sensor is easily swamped by the Earth's field and nearby equipment; several sensors working differentially are needed for real environments.
